title: Remote checkpoint checksum ripples — intermittent load failures
body:
Summary:
Observed intermittent model load failures across a subset of hosts where a small percentage (~0.5-1%) of checkpoint loads fail with checksum mismatches or tar-errors. Failures look bursty and sometimes correlate with high concurrency during nightly model rollouts. This is a personal investigation log — hand-off notes for infra/serving to harden fetch/verify path.

Symptoms (examples):
- 2024-09-10T03:22:41Z — worker-a log: "Checksum mismatch for shard weights-00023.bin (expected sha256: 6a3f..., got: 2c1b...)"
- 2024-09-12T11:05:17Z — worker-f: "tar: Unexpected EOF in archive" while streaming tarball from gs://model-checkpoints/prod/v3/model-20240911.tgz
- 2024-09-15T02:40:03Z — ephemeral host: requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError during streaming download (stack trace snippet below).

Commands / quick repro I ran locally: (ran from a jump host in same region, replicates the problem sometimes)
- gsutil stat gs://model-checkpoints/prod/v3/model-20240911.tgz
  -> Creation: 2024-09-11T18:45:01Z
  -> MD5: XXXXXX (note: gsutil shows md5, GCS stores crc32c too)
- gsutil cat gs://model-checkpoints/prod/v3/model-20240911.tgz | sha256sum
  -> intermittent: returned sha256 that doesn't match the MD5-derived expected (we don't store sha256 in metadata, so I compute from canonical artifact)
- gsutil hash -m gs://model-checkpoints/prod/v3/model-20240911.tgz
  -> output: md5:..., crc32c:..., size: 3,145,728,512
- curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://storage.googleapis.com/model-checkpoints/prod/v3/model-20240911.tgz"
  -> 200 OK (headers include x-goog-generation and x-goog-metageneration)

Representative error snippets copied from logs: (redacted host ids)
- Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/opt/serving/runtime/loader.py", line 412, in _stream_and_verify
      for chunk in resp.iter_content(chunk_size=65536):
    File "/usr/lib/python3.11/site-packages/requests/models.py", line 837, in iter_content
      raise ChunkedEncodingError(e)
  requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError: ("Connection broken: IncompleteRead(16384 bytes read, 32768 more expected)")

- tar: Unexpected EOF in archive
  tar: Error is not recoverable: exiting now

- loader: manifest-shard-check failed: expected 128 shards for layer 5; found 127
  loader: computed_checksum mismatch for weights-00086.bin (expected sha256 \"a1b2c3\", got \"000000\")

What I verified / hypotheses so far:
1) Partial object written / truncated reads: some symptoms point to truncated downloads (tar EOF, IncompleteRead). This could be network/NAT or a transient GCS server issue.
2) Stale/corrupt objects on GCS: possibility that an earlier upload was interrupted and later replaced inconsistently; GCS has object metageneration and generation but we don't assert them currently.
3) CDN / caching layer serving stale slices: if intermediate caches return partial or different bytes during a rollout we could get inconsistent checksums.
4) Client-side streaming code insufficiently defensive: requests.iter_content with no per-chunk size enforcement and we don't re-request missing ranges when a read returns fewer bytes than expected.
5) Concurrency + parallel downloads race with delete/rewrite of the same object during pruning/retention tasks (e.g., a background job replaced model artifact while some hosts were mid-download) — leads to missing shard in archive.

Things I tried (and results):
- Re-downloaded multiple times in a loop to attempt to reproduce flakiness: ~40 runs, 2 reproductions where sha256 differed from the canonical artifact (same region, same host).
- gsutil -m cp to local then sha256sum: cp sometimes fails with "Read error" matching the ChunkedEncodingError.
- curl with range requests for the final 64KB of the tarball: some times range request returns correct bytes, other times 502/503.
- Verified server-side generation/metageneration (x-goog-generation) returned identical values across two hosts for the same object at the same timestamp — suggests object was not replaced at that instant.
- Ran checksum on individual shard files after extracting: when tar extraction fails we sometimes still have partially written shard files. The corrupt ones often show a run of null bytes at the end.

Quick local mitigation I added to loader (branch: GH PR reference above):
- Add per-chunk length expectation and re-request range for missing bytes up to 3 retries with exponential backoff.
- Expand verification: compute crc32c and compare against GCS crc32c header (when available) as a quick integrity check before unpacking.
- Fail-fast on inconsistent generation headers (x-goog-generation mismatch between HEAD and later GET).

Open questions / items to investigate:
- Are there any in-flight uploads/GC jobs that run around midnight that might rewrite artifacts without atomic swaps? Check infra-retention job schedule.
- Does our upload pipeline use resumable uploads that sometimes leave a zero-padded tail on object finalization? (ask data pipeline team)
- Could NAT gateway scaling cause connection resets that manifests as truncated stream? (SRE follow-up)
- Is there any service that re-encrypts/re-writes objects (e.g., KMS rotation) that could cause transient reads?

Additional diagnostics to run (planned):
- Add server and client side logging of x-goog-generation + crc32c + content-length on every HEAD/GET and surface diffs in error reports.
- Instrumented small binary that downloads file in fixed ranges and compares each range against a golden copy; run from multiple AZs/hosts concurrently for an hour to try to reproduce pattern.
- Schedule a repeat of nightly rollout with additional debug logging enabled on a small rollout cohort to capture a failing host live.

Manual commands for extra checks (notes to self):
- gsutil stat -a gs://model-checkpoints/prod/v3/model-20240911.tgz
- gsutil hash -h gs://model-checkpoints/prod/v3/model-20240911.tgz   # compute checks across algorithms
- python -c "import requests; r=requests.get(\"https://storage.googleapis.com/model-checkpoints/prod/v3/model-20240911.tgz\", stream=True); print(r.headers.get('x-goog-generation'), r.headers.get('x-goog-metageneration')); chunk=next(r.iter_content(65536)); print(len(chunk))"  # quick stream sample

Possible long-term fixes:
- Store and serve a sidecar manifest that includes per-shard sha256 (not just tar-level md5/crc). Clients verify each shard file after extraction and before use.
- Use a two-phase upload for artifacts: upload to tmp path then atomic rename (compose) to final path to avoid mid-download replacements.
- Add server-side signed range URLs to clients and implement robust range-retry logic.
- Harden client to detect and retry ETag/generation mismatches before attempting to unpack.

Next steps (owner: Lucy, collaborators Arjun/Maya):
- [ ] Arjun: check infra retention/cleanup job timings and any recent changes to upload pipeline (by 2024-10-07).
- [ ] Maya: run the range-check binary from 10 hosts across 2 regions to attempt repro (by 2024-10-05).
- [ ] Lucy: push the small verification patch to the staging rollout and enable debug logging for 10% of loads (PR #728) (by 2024-10-04).
- [ ] SRE: confirm NAT gateway metrics and any connection-reset patterns around the failure windows (link to SRE ticket requested).

Notes to whoever picks this up:
- Keep the artifact hashes and generation headers in any bug report. They are usually the key to correlating client-side partial reads with server-side state.
- If you see zero-filled tails in shards, that's a strong signal of truncated upload or in-flight replacement; keep a copy and grep for trailing null bytes.
- I've left a small harness in /home/lucy/checksum-harness (private) that can be copied to a k8s job for larger scale repro.

Last manual test run summary (2024-10-01):
- 200 download attempts across 5 hosts over 6 hours: 3 reproductions (1.5%) with truncated reads; generation headers matched in 2/3 reproductions, differed in 1/3. Suggests multiple root causes.

If you need context: see linked JIRA (INF-3421) and the PR with the defensive changes. Slack thread has some raw logs.

-- Lucy
